split_reasoning: Inquiries arrive both as live contacts (phone, walk-up, chat) and as written tickets or emails, and these are different kinds of item (a live resolved conversation versus a written answer), so split by channel.

parts.text: Answer a user's live inquiry (phone, chat, or walk-up) about software or hardware operation and resolve the problem.
parts.type_reasoning: The work is a live conversation with a user that ends in a resolved request and a ticket record.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each call or walk-up contact is logged and closed as one ticket at the help desk.
parts.work_item: one user call or walk-up inquiry resolved
parts.start: user's call, chat, or walk-up request
parts.end: user confirms the problem is resolved (or it is escalated), ticket logged
parts.checked_by: the user; help desk lead via ticket review

parts.text: Answer a user's written inquiry (email or ticket) about software or hardware operation to resolve the problem.
parts.type_reasoning: Each inquiry produces a written answer the user relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Written inquiries enter the ticket queue one at a time and are closed individually.
parts.work_item: one emailed or ticketed user inquiry answered
parts.end: answer sent, user confirms or ticket auto-closes

notes: Channel split shares are a judgment; 1288 covers the troubleshooting behind the same tickets, so the two statements substantially overlap.

split_reasoning: One activity: running commands and observing a system to confirm it works or find errors.

parts.text: Run commands and observe a system or workstation to verify it operates correctly and detect errors.
parts.type_reasoning: Each check ends in a verified system or a logged error that others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Verification is done per system, typically after an install or repair or as a scheduled check, and recorded once.
parts.work_item: one system or workstation verification check
parts.start: install/repair completed or scheduled check due
parts.end: system confirmed working, or error recorded and ticket opened
parts.checked_by: user of the system; supervisor or ticket reviewer

notes: Could be read as a step within installation/repair (1284) or daily oversight (1285) rather than a standalone item.

split_reasoning: Hardware and peripheral installation or repair is hands-on physical work, while software installation or repair is done at a computer, so split.

parts.text: Install or perform minor repairs on computer hardware or peripheral equipment following specifications.
parts.type_reasoning: Requires hands-on work with physical equipment away from a desk.

parts.text: Install or repair software on a user's machine following installation specifications.
parts.type_reasoning: Each install or fix produces a working configuration the user relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Software installs and fixes are requested and closed as individual tickets.
parts.work_item: one software install or repair request completed
parts.start: install or repair request ticket assigned
parts.end: software installed/fixed and tested, ticket closed

notes: Shares between hardware and software depend heavily on the site; software installs also overlap with new-employee setup in 1286.

split_reasoning: Overseeing performance is ongoing; it produces two kinds of item: routine daily checks and investigation of specific performance issues.

parts.text: Carry out the daily check of computer system performance and record its status.
parts.type_reasoning: Recast from ongoing oversight; each daily check produces a status record others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The check is done and logged once per day per set of systems.
parts.start: start of the day's monitoring review
parts.end: status logged, any issues opened as tickets

parts.text: Investigate a system performance issue or alert and take or request corrective action.
parts.type_reasoning: Recast from ongoing oversight; each issue ends in a decision and a ticket note.
parts.unit_reasoning: Issues and alerts are the unit that enters the queue and gets closed.
parts.work_item: one performance issue or alert investigated
parts.end: cause recorded and fix applied, escalated, or closed as no action

notes: For a user support specialist 'oversee' is loosely defined; shares are a judgment.

split_reasoning: Setting up equipment combines physical placement and cabling with installing the operating system and software at a computer, so split per the physical/computer rule.

parts.text: Physically set up equipment at an employee's workstation and install or check cables.
parts.type_reasoning: Hands-on work placing hardware and running cables.

parts.text: Install and configure the operating system and required software on an employee's new machine.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a configured machine that the employee relies on and that can be checked.
parts.unit_reasoning: New-hire or replacement setups are requested and signed off per machine.
parts.work_item: one employee machine imaged and configured
parts.start: setup request for a new employee or replacement machine
parts.end: machine configured with OS, software, and accounts; handed to employee and ticket closed

notes: 'Ensuring proper installation' may mean supervising others' setup, which would be interpersonal; coded as doing it oneself.

split_reasoning: Record-keeping is ongoing and covers three different kinds of record: problem/remedy records, installation records, and logs of daily data communication transactions.

parts.text: Write the record of a problem and the remedial action taken.
parts.type_reasoning: Recast from ongoing record-keeping; each record is a distinct item others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Records are written per incident, as the ticket's resolution notes.
parts.work_item: one incident record (problem and remedy) written
parts.end: record entered in the ticket or log system
parts.checked_by: help desk lead; colleagues handling later incidents

parts.text: Record an installation activity (equipment or software installed, where and for whom).
parts.type_reasoning: Recast from ongoing record-keeping; each installation entry is a distinct record.
parts.unit_reasoning: Installation entries are made per install in the asset or change log.

parts.text: Compile the daily log of data communication transactions.
parts.type_reasoning: Recast from ongoing record-keeping; each daily log is a distinct record.
parts.unit_reasoning: The log is compiled and closed out once per day.
parts.work_item: one daily data communication transaction log

notes: Part a is often written as the closing step of tickets counted under 1282/1288; the daily transaction log may be rare in modern settings.

split_reasoning: One activity, resolving a problem or providing support, done by alternative means (manuals, conferring, diagnostics).

parts.text: Investigate and resolve a user's technical problem using manuals, discussion with the user, or diagnostics.
parts.type_reasoning: Each investigation ends in a resolved problem and ticket record that the user and team rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Problems are handled and closed as individual tickets.
parts.work_item: one technical problem ticket investigated and resolved
parts.end: fix applied and confirmed, resolution recorded, ticket closed

notes: Heavily overlaps with 1282; the line between answering an inquiry and investigating a problem is blurry.

split_reasoning: One activity: meeting with stakeholders to establish requirements.

parts.text: Confer with staff, users, and management to establish requirements for new systems or modifications.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the meetings themselves; the instructions treat setting requirements with staff as interpersonal.

notes: Meetings may produce a written requirements note, which would be a checkable deliverable.

split_reasoning: Two different activities joined by 'or': writing training materials and procedures, and training users.

parts.text: Develop a training guide or procedure document for using hardware or software.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a document that users and colleagues rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Guides and procedures are written and published one at a time.
parts.work_item: one training guide or procedure document
parts.end: document reviewed and published to users or the knowledge base
parts.checked_by: IT supervisor; users who follow it

parts.text: Train users in the proper use of hardware or software.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the live training session; nothing a colleague would check is produced.

split_reasoning: One activity: escalating a problem or defective product to an outside party.

parts.text: Refer a major hardware or software problem or a defective product to a vendor or technician for service.
parts.type_reasoning: Each referral produces a vendor case or escalation record that others act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Referrals are handed over as one vendor case, RMA, or escalated ticket.
parts.work_item: one problem escalated to a vendor or technician
parts.start: decision that the problem exceeds in-house repair
parts.end: vendor case or RMA opened with details, service arranged, user informed

notes: Includes a phone call with the vendor in some cases, but the deliverable is the case record.

split_reasoning: One deliverable: an evaluation with recommendations; evaluating and recommending are parts of the same report.

parts.text: Evaluate a piece of software or hardware and recommend improvements or upgrades.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a written evaluation that managers read and act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The evaluation is handed over and decided on as one document.
parts.start: request or need to assess a product or upgrade
parts.end: evaluation and recommendation sent to manager

split_reasoning: One activity: keeping knowledge current by alternative means (reading, conferences).

parts.text: Read trade magazines and manuals or attend conferences to maintain knowledge of hardware and software.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces nothing anyone else checks or relies on.

split_reasoning: One activity: preparing equipment for delivery; reading the order sheet is part of checking the equipment against it.

parts.text: Inspect equipment against order sheets and prepare it for delivery to users.
parts.type_reasoning: Requires hands-on handling and inspection of physical equipment.

notes: Reading the order sheet is a small desk component not split out.

split_reasoning: One activity: modifying commercial software for internal use.

parts.text: Modify or customize a commercial program to meet an internal need.
parts.type_reasoning: Each customization produces a working change users rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Customizations are requested, built, tested, and released one at a time.
parts.work_item: one customization of a commercial program delivered
parts.start: customization request from a user group
parts.end: change tested and released to users

split_reasoning: One deliverable, a feasibility study; workflow analysis, space design, and cost comparison are components of it.

parts.text: Conduct an office automation feasibility study including workflow analysis, space design, or cost comparison.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a study report that management reads and decides on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The study is handed over and signed off as one report.
parts.work_item: one office automation feasibility study report
parts.start: management request to assess an automation option
parts.end: report with analysis and recommendation delivered to management

notes: Larger in scope than a single deliverable may suggest; site visits for space design may involve some physical work.

split_reasoning: Two different activities: hiring workers, and supervising and directing them.

parts.text: Hire workers for special project, problem-solving, monitoring, and installation work.
parts.type_reasoning: Hiring is done through interviews and live judgment; the value is in the interaction.

parts.text: Supervise and direct workers engaged in special project, problem-solving, monitoring, and installation work.
parts.type_reasoning: Supervising and directing is interpersonal; nothing a colleague would check is produced.

notes: Hiring may produce a hiring recommendation document, but the core work is interviewing.
